title: Ops Utility Stitcher and Chaos-safe Playground for Runbooks-as-Tasks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current runbook fragments and admin snippets are useful but scattered. On-call engineers and SREs repeatedly compose ad-hoc sequences during incidents, which causes variability, manual errors, and audit gaps. We need an ergonomics-first system that stitches verified snippet fragments into executable task-graphs, and a sandboxed playground to validate the stitched flows against synthetic incidents and chaos scenarios before promoting to production.

Proposal summary: Build an "Ops Utility Stitcher" service that: 1) discovers and catalogs typed runbook snippets (existing snippet store), 2) provides a visual authoring surface that composes snippets into a task graph with typed inputs/outputs, 3) injects safety checks (RBAC gating, rate/impact estimates, preflight dry-run checks), and 4) runs composed flows in a "Chaos-safe Playground" which can simulate downstream service failures, permission denials, and latency spikes. The stitcher will persist canonical artifacts (versioned runbook-tasks) and expose an operator API for execution in the runbooks-as-tasks runtime.

Why different from current work: Many existing efforts focus on converting runbooks to tasks or creating miniagents; this proposal emphasizes a test-first, simulation-first pipeline (the playground) and explicit stitcher metadata (impact budget, external side-effect descriptors) so composed flows are automatically classified for training, auditing, and telemetry. The goal is to reduce incident MTTR variability and make automation promotions safer.

Key design constraints: maintain idempotency by default; require explicit strong-typed outputs for each snippet; keep per-step side-effect descriptors (read-only, write-limited, destructive) and an impact score. Integrated with RBAC so only owners or SREs can promote to production. Minimal runtime changes: composed flows are translated to our existing runlet/task runner (no new execution engine).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Stitcher prototype that can import at least 50 existing snippets and produce a composable task graph via UI or API.
2) Playground can execute a dry-run of a composed flow against synthetic test doubles and report safety violations (e.g., destructive action without approval, external service not-mocked).
3) Promotion gating: only runs that pass the playground's safety checks and have required approvals can be marked 'canary-ready'.
4) Generated artifacts include metadata (version, owner, impact_score, allowed_environments) that the runtime and console can consume.
5) Integration tests: 10 automated scenarios covering permission failure, downstream timeout, partial success rollbacks.
6) Telemetry emitted for executed flows: token counts, latency per step, error classification, and approval history links.
implementation_notes:
Phases: 
- Phase 1 (MVP): Stitcher backend + simple React authoring UI, import adapter for current snippet repo, export to runtime-compatible JSON (task graph). Playground runs confined to a k8s namespace with mocked service endpoints (chaos scenarios implemented via traffic-shaping and fault-injection sidecars).
- Phase 2: Approvals + RBAC integration (SSO/SAML group mapping), impact scoring automation, and per-step rollback recipes.
- Phase 3: Console integration (listing promoted runbook-tasks, telemetry panels), scheduler integration for periodic smoke-tests.

Implementation details: 
- Use existing snippet schema but add fields: "impact_score" (0-100), "side_effects" (list), "required_approvals" (list), "mock_strategy" (none|light|full). These are stored as YAML blobs in snippet registry.
- Translation step emits a flattened DAG with explicit edges and typed inputs. The runtime will consume the DAG and run steps sequentially or in parallel based on annotations.
- Playground harness: implement a controller that spins ephemeral mock endpoints (from a paramizable scenarios library) and a failure injector that can simulate TCP resets, 503s, and auth failures. Use HashiCorp Nomad or a constrained k8s namespace (TBD) for isolation.
- Safety checks: static lint for missing side_effects, required_approvals; approximate cost estimator using our token/unit heuristics; criticality flag that prevents promotion unless SRE-approved.

Trade-offs and decisions: 
- Execution engine reuse vs new runtime: decided to reuse runlet runner to reduce maintenance burden. This constrains some advanced pause/resume semantics, which we'll emulate via wrapper steps.
- Full-fidelity mocks vs lightweight fakes: start with lightweight fakes (status codes, latency injection), add full-service simulators later.

Progress notes:
- Discovery: catalog export script written (ENG-995001-catalog-export) and run against current snippet store; ~72 snippets discovered, 54 compatible with typed-output schema.
- Prototype UI: wireframes reviewed by Design (see link). Feedback: expose side_effects and impact score prominently; add 'what-if' toggle for destructive steps.
- PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-stitcher/pull/23 (WIP).

Risks: 
- False sense of safety if playground mocks are insufficient — mitigated by conservative promotion defaults.
- RBAC surface complexity — will require security review and one-week slot from infra.

Open questions: 
- Should the impact_score be auto-derived from historical telemetry? (TBD; planned for Phase 2)
- Persistent storage: use existing snippet registry or separate DB? (Using existing registry for MVP.)
testing_plan:
Unit tests for translation and lint rules; integration harness that runs 12 synthetic scenarios in the playground (permission denied, downstream 503, partial failure with rollback, network partition, high latency, auth timeout). Canary: pick one non-critical runbook that remediates a non-production-only alarm; run it in canary mode against the playground then in a scoped staging environment. Failure criteria: any run that requires manual operator intervention during canary fails and reverts promotion.

QA tasks: 
- Write scenario definitions as JSON files (stored under /ops-stitcher/scenarios).
- Add CI job that runs playground scenarios on every merge to main.
- Smoke dashboards to surface errors and step-level latencies.
rollout_plan:
1) Internal alpha: core SRE + 2 support engineers test the authoring UI and run 20 curated scenarios (week 1).
2) Expanded beta: product support and two service teams invited to author 5 real runbook-tasks each (weeks 2-5).
3) Promotion rules applied: only runbooks passing playground and SRE sign-off can be scheduled in production; bulk-imported snippets remain read-only until owners opt-in.
4) Metrics to watch: % automated promotions, average MTTR variance across incidents, number of reverts.

Monitoring: Console will have a dedicated "Stitcher" dashboard; cross-link each promoted task to execution telemetry and approval history. Rollback: at first sign of systemic misbehavior we will immediately disable promotions and revoke canary tokens.
